subject: CareHive POC: scope, success gates, and eval approach
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@carehive.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: CareHive POC: scope, success gates, and eval approach

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock a POC path that matches your evaluation needs. I attached a draft POC charter (CareHive_POC_Charter_v1.pdf).

Recap (from today's discovery)
- Primary goal: reduce triage time for nurse intake by surfacing relevant patient context (chief complaint + meds + allergies) to care coordinators.
- Data constraints: PHI present; CareHive expects only tokenized extracts to leave the VPC during the POC.
- Volume target: ~5k patient notes/week; sample dataset of ~2k notes for offline eval.

Proposed POC scope and timeline
- 4-week POC: week 0 kickoff + data handoff, week 1 offline eval, week 2 shadow integration, week 3 live shadow + acceptance scoring, week 4 review and decision.
- Owners: CareHive PM (Tom) provides dataset + success feedback; Redwood SE (Marissa) owns offline eval and rubric; SRE (Ben) owns shadow integration and latency monitoring.

Initial suggested success gates (we'll refine together):
- Accuracy: extract precision >= 85% on key fields (cc/meds/allergies) on offline holdout
- Hallucination: <1% clinically significant hallucinations on manual spot checks
- Latency: p95 inference <500ms in shadow mode
- Business metric: 20% reduction in average triage time in measured shadow sessions

Eval methodology options (we discussed briefly):
A) Offline-only: Redwood runs eval on a labeled holdout dataset we process in your VPC (safe for PHI) — faster to iterate but less representative of live traffic.
B) Online shadow: run model in parallel with production routing; compare outputs to human baseline — higher fidelity, needs careful safety controls and SRE work.

Ask: which approach do you prefer? If you want high-fidelity results, we recommend a hybrid: offline experiments first to gate quality, then a short controlled shadow to validate latency and end-to-end behavior.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm dataset availability and whether we can run the offline pass in your VPC (preferred).
2) Marissa will share a first-pass rubric CSV for scoring (attached separately).
3) If you agree, lock kickoff for Tue Jul 20.

Attached: CareHive_POC_Charter_v1.pdf

Thanks — excited to move forward.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
chloe@redwood.com

From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@carehive.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@carehive.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CareHive POC: scope, success gates, and eval approach

Chloe —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- Dataset: we can provide the 2k-note holdout by Mon Jul 19; it will be in our secure S3 with KMS. We prefer the offline pass to happen in our VPC (no data egress).
- PHI constraints: no patient-identifiable text may be stored outside our environment. If Redwood can run the eval in our environment (Redwood Private or via temporary secure job), that works.
- Metrics: precision on extracted fields is important; also please include a recall metric (we care about missed critical meds).

Regarding offline vs shadow: we like the hybrid recommendation. We are risk-averse: start with offline to tune, then a 1-week limited shadow against 10% of sessions. Shadow must strip any PII from logs and have an opt-out flag for clinicians.

One ask: can you share the rubric CSV you mentioned and a short matrix showing how you weight clinical risk vs precision vs latency? That will help our legal and clinical reviewers.

Tom and I are generally available Tue Jul 20 for a kickoff.

Best,
Sarah Nguyen
Head of Product
CareHive
sarah@carehive.com

Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: CareHive POC — technical feasibility notes

Team — quick internal note after reviewing the charter and the constraints Sarah mentioned. High-level recommendations:

1) Hybrid eval path:
   - Phase 1 (offline): run token-level extract/classification tests against your labeled holdout inside CareHive VPC. This validates extraction accuracy and recall with zero live exposure.
   - Phase 2 (limited shadow): 7 days at 10% traffic, read-only outputs, no storage of identifiable outputs; strict logging controls and automatic redaction.

2) Ownership and tasks:
   - Marissa (SE): build the evaluation pipeline and the rubric, own offline pass and manual spot-checks.
   - Ben (SRE): provision a transient shadow route, add latency/throughput dashboards, define fail-open thresholds.
   - Karthik (Solutions): confirm model variants and quantization profile to meet p95 targets.

3) Scoring guidance (initial):
   - Use a weighted score: 0.5 extraction F1 (average across key fields), 0.3 clinical-safety score (manual audit on a sample), 0.2 ops score (latency p95 normalized).
   - Preliminary pass threshold: weighted_score >= 0.8 for go/no-go to limited shadow.

Risks / blockers:
- Legal needs to sign the data processing agreement for an in-VPC job.
- If we cannot run inside their VPC, we can accept a thoroughly redacted dataset but will lose fidelity.

I'll prepare a short tech runbook for Ben and Marissa today.

-karthik

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@carehive.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@carehive.com>

Date: Thu, 14 Jul 2027 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: CareHive POC — evaluation rubric and scoring thresholds (attached)

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Per Chloe and Karthik's notes, attached is the evaluation rubric CSV (carehive_evaluation_rubric_v1.csv) and a short summary below. This is designed to be runnable in your environment and to give a clear, auditable score for each model variant.

Summary of rubric and scoring rules:
- Fields scored: chief_complaint, medication_list, allergies.
- Per-field metrics: precision, recall, F1.
- Clinical-safety audit: random sample of 100 outputs reviewed by a clinician; each clinically significant hallucination = -0.05 to the safety subscore.

Weighted scoring (0-1 scale):
- Extraction F1 average (fields) * 0.50
- Clinical-safety pass rate (1 - normalized hallucination penalty) * 0.30
- Ops (latency p95 target 450ms) normalized to 0-1 * 0.20

Pass criteria (proposed):
- Weighted_score >= 0.80 AND
- Hallucination rate (clinically significant) < 1% AND
- Latency p95 < 450ms

Proposed POC timeline & immediate next steps:
- Mon Jul 19: CareHive provides labeled holdout (S3 link + IAM role).
- Tue Jul 20 (kickoff): data transfer validation + runbook review.
- Wed Jul 21 to Fri Jul 23: offline eval and rubric scoring.
- Mon Jul 26 to Sun Aug 1: limited shadow (10% traffic).
- Mon Aug 2: final scoring, review, and commercial decision.

Attachments: carehive_evaluation_rubric_v1.csv

Questions for CareHive:
1) Can legal sign the needed DPA for an in-VPC transient job, or do you prefer a redacted export?
2) Is a 10% shadow acceptable operationally? We can reduce to 5% if they want more conservative rollout.

If that looks good we'll lock the kickoff for Tue Jul 20 at 10am PT.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
